title: Kingdom of Sardinia
capsule: The Kingdom of Sardinia in its Savoyard phase (1720–1861) originated when Victor Amadeus II of Savoy exchanged Sicily for Sardinia under the Treaty of The Hague (1720), unifying his mainland Piedmontese holdings with the island under a single crown headquartered in Turin. The kingdom adopted the Statuto Albertino constitutional charter in 1848 and became the engine of Italian unification under Prime Minister Camillo di Cavour, who allied with Napoleon III against Austria in 1859, winning Lombardy by the Peace of Zurich. The rapid annexations of central Italian states and Garibaldi's conquest of the Two Sicilies (1860) consolidated the peninsula; on 17 March 1861 the parliament of Turin proclaimed the Kingdom of Italy, with Victor Emmanuel II continuing as king.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's borders are well documented through treaty records and cartographic sources, though the Savoyard-Piedmontese mainland territories changed repeatedly through dynastic and Napoleonic rearrangements before stabilizing in 1815.
